thread:
Priya (Product): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands 1 — want to capture a few clarifications on positioning + roadmap so teams can act. @Ari @Sam tiny answers pls.
Ari (CEO): happy to. keep them coming, will be concise.
Priya (Product): 1) What's the single sentence we should lead with for the website vs sales decks?
Ari (CEO): Website: 'Predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.' Sales deck: start with customer outcomes: 'Lower inference cost, predictable latency, and deployment flexibility for regulated & mission-critical apps.'
Lucas (Growth): nit: should marketing use "inference" or "LLM serving"? engineers care, PMs might not.
Ari (CEO): Use "inference" broadly; add "LLM serving" in tech-facing assets.
Priya (Product): 2) Competitors — how do we frame differences vs cloud vendor endpoints and vs API-first LLM providers?
Sam (CTO): Cloud endpoints = commodity infra; they provide VMs and GPUs. We provide an opinionated runtime + routing/caching/rollouts that reduces per-token cost and operational complexity. API-first LLM providers = model access + freshness; we compete on predictable economics and hybrid deployment options (private/VPC/Dedicated).
Mei (Sales): any objection to messaging that we "replace" cloud endpoints for latency-sensitive apps?
Ari (CEO): Don't say "replace" outright. Say "complement or replace depending on needs" — it's less antagonistic and more honest.
Priya (Product): 3) Mission clarity: are we exclusively optimizing for inference throughput/cost or are we also owning model quality (fine-tuning/evals) as a product pillar?
Sam (CTO): Primary focus remains inference & ops. We enable model quality through integrations: model index, verified perf profiles, and an evals pipeline customers can plug into. We won't be a full model training platform.
Nora (Finance): from a revenue perspective, will we price any model-quality addons separately?
Ari (CEO): yes — advanced evals/quality-monitoring and long-term retention for audit logs will be add-ons or enterprise features.
Priya (Product): 4) Roadmap calls: what are the most urgent features that impact close rates for Dedicated in next 60 days?
Mei (Sales): low hanging: dedicated autoscaling SLA docs + an onboarding checklist for SOC/infosec. also a simple TCO calculator for Dedicated vs self-host.
Ari (CEO): agree. shipping the autoscale policy + the TCO calc is top priority.
Sam (CTO): engineering addendum: we also need a predictable capacity demo that shows tail latency under load. we can build a replay harness using real request traces.
Priya (Product): 5) Metrics we should watch month-to-month?
Lucas (Growth): Hosted: activation -> paid conversion, MAU dev accounts, and cost per active customer. Dedicated: deal velocity, time to first unit (onboarding time), churn/NRR.
Priya (Product): one procedural Q — if an engineer wants to propose a model variant (higher-quality but higher-cost) for default in Dedicated, who signs off?
Sam (CTO): eng + ML infra lead + product + the assigned AE for the customer. include perf and cost delta in PRD.
Priya (Product): last: any red flags teams should stop doing?
Ari (CEO): avoid feature-scope creep that compromises latency SLAs. experiments encouraged, but protect production SLOs.
Mei (Sales): can we get a 1-pager summarizing these answers to share with prospects?
Priya (Product): will draft and share by EOD tomorrow.
